title: UN Arms Embargo Strangles Bosnia
narrative: The UN arms embargo, originally imposed on all of Yugoslavia, disproportionately impacts the fledgling Bosnian government. While the VRS inherits vast JNA stockpiles and the HVO receives supplies from Croatia, the ARBiH faces severe weapons shortages across all fronts.

effects.text: The UN arms embargo leaves the ARBiH critically short of weapons and ammunition.

title: JNA Forces Begin Withdrawal from Bosnia
narrative: The Yugoslav People's Army formally announces its withdrawal from Bosnia-Herzegovina. In practice, Bosnian Serb personnel simply change insignia, and massive quantities of heavy weapons, ammunition depots, and military infrastructure are transferred directly to the newly formed VRS.

effects.text: The JNA formally withdraws from Bosnia. Equipment, bases, and ammunition stores are left to the VRS.

title: Siege of Sarajevo Intensifies
narrative: The SRK tightens its grip around Sarajevo as artillery bombardment from surrounding hills intensifies. The city's 350,000 residents face daily shelling, sniper fire, and the severing of water and electricity supplies. The siege becomes the longest in modern European warfare.

effect.text: Sarajevo is encircled. The SRK begins systematic bombardment from positions on the surrounding hills.

title: First UN Aid Convoys Enter Bosnia
narrative: UNHCR organizes the first humanitarian aid convoys into besieged areas of Bosnia. The convoys face obstruction at Serb checkpoints and are frequently diverted or looted. Despite the difficulties, a fragile lifeline begins to form for trapped civilian populations.

effect.text: The first UN humanitarian convoys reach besieged populations, establishing a fragile supply lifeline.

title: Srebrenica Pocket Crystallizes
narrative: Under the command of Naser Oric, Bosniak forces in the Drina Valley consolidate a defensive perimeter around Srebrenica. Despite being vastly outgunned, local TDF fighters and volunteers launch raids on surrounding VRS positions, establishing a tenuous enclave that shelters tens of thousands of displaced civilians.

effects.text: Bosniak forces consolidate around Srebrenica, forming a besieged enclave that becomes a symbol of resistance.

title: HVO and ARBiH Jointly Liberate Mostar
narrative: In a rare display of cooperation, HVO and ARBiH forces jointly drive the JNA from Mostar after weeks of fierce fighting. The city is liberated but not unified — the HVO quickly asserts control over the western bank while the ARBiH consolidates in the east. The seeds of a future division are planted even in the moment of shared victory.

effects.text: Mostar is liberated from the JNA. HVO and ARBiH celebrate together, but the HVO moves quickly to assert control over the western bank.

title: Operation Corridor — VRS Breaks Through at Brcko
narrative: The VRS launches Operation Corridor to link the Krajina region with Serbia proper through the narrow Posavina corridor near Brcko. Fierce fighting against HVO and ARBiH forces gradually widens the corridor, establishing a critical supply and communication link that sustains the western Bosnian Serb entity.

effect.text: The VRS secures the Posavina Corridor near Brcko, linking Krajina with Serbia. A vital supply artery is established.

title: Drina Valley Campaign Accelerates
narrative: VRS and paramilitary forces systematically expel the Bosniak population from towns along the Drina River valley. Visegrad, Foca, Zvornik, and Bratunac witness mass killings, forced deportations, and the destruction of mosques. The campaign aims to create a contiguous Serb-held corridor along the Serbian border.

effects.text: Systematic ethnic cleansing sweeps through the Drina Valley. Tens of thousands of Bosniaks are expelled or killed.

title: Posavina Corridor Fighting Intensifies
narrative: Control of the narrow Posavina corridor remains hotly contested. The HVO and ARBiH launch repeated counterattacks to sever the VRS supply line, while Serb forces fight to widen and secure the passage. The corridor near Brcko narrows at points to barely a few kilometers wide.

effects.text: VRS reinforces and widens the Posavina Corridor. The supply line to Krajina stabilizes despite continued pressure.

title: Concentration Camps Exposed to the World
narrative: British journalists gain access to the Omarska and Trnopolje detention camps near Prijedor. Images of emaciated prisoners behind barbed wire shock the international community and draw direct comparisons to the Holocaust. The revelations trigger global outrage and demands for intervention.

effects.text: Images of Omarska and Trnopolje camps shock the world. International pressure on the Bosnian Serb leadership intensifies dramatically.

title: Bihac Pocket Increasingly Isolated
narrative: The Bihac pocket in northwestern Bosnia becomes increasingly cut off from the rest of government-held territory. The 5th Corps under General Atif Dudakovic maintains a resilient defense, but supply shortages and the presence of Fikret Abdic's autonomous enclave in Velika Kladusa complicate the military and political situation.

effect.text: The Bihac pocket grows more isolated. The 5th Corps defends stubbornly but faces supply shortages and internal division.

title: London Conference on Yugoslavia
narrative: The international community convenes in London to address the escalating Bosnian crisis. Western leaders demand an end to ethnic cleansing and the lifting of sieges. The conference produces declarations but no enforcement mechanism, establishing a pattern of diplomatic engagement without military commitment.

effect.text: The London Conference demands ceasefire and end to ethnic cleansing. All parties face pressure to comply.

response_options.label: Accept Conference Terms
response_options.description: Signal willingness to negotiate. Improves international standing but may constrain military operations.

response_options.label: Reject Terms as Inadequate
response_options.description: Denounce the conference as rewarding aggression. Damages credibility but preserves freedom of action.

title: HVO-ARBiH Clash at Prozor
narrative: The fragile alliance between the HVO and ARBiH fractures openly at Prozor in central Bosnia. HVO forces attack Bosniak civilians and ARBiH positions in a calculated bid to assert Croat control over the town. Further clashes erupt near Novi Travnik. The incidents mark the first serious military confrontation between the two nominal allies.

effects.text: HVO and ARBiH forces clash at Prozor and Novi Travnik. The fragile alliance between Croats and Bosniaks shows deepening cracks.

title: Jajce Falls to VRS Forces
narrative: The strategic town of Jajce in central Bosnia falls to the VRS after a prolonged siege. The loss is a major blow to both the ARBiH and HVO, who blame each other for failing to coordinate the defense. Tens of thousands of civilians flee westward, and recriminations between the two forces deepen the growing rift.

effects.text: Jajce falls to the VRS. Mutual blame between HVO and ARBiH accelerates the breakdown of their alliance.
